verdict.rationale: Recurly's own docs name Account Updater and Expired Card Management as involuntary-churn tools, and describe backup payment methods that keep service running when the primary payment fails. There is no evidence of a hosted update-payment page; the Engage payment-failure flow uses in-app prompts, which is a different feature. Missing for 10: hosted update-payment page evidence, detail on how Account Updater works with card networks (coverage, automation), independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ops user, expiring or replaced cards update themselves — network account updater, backup payment methods, and hosted update-payment pages

citations.quote: Reduce involuntary customer churn in Recurly through Account Updater, Intelligent Retries, Dunning Campaigns, Expired Card Management, and backup payment methods.
Let customers designate a backup payment method so service continues automatically if their primary payment fails.

Involuntary churn happens when customers are lost due to factors outside their intent — expired cards, bank changes, or failed payments. Recurly provides several tools to proactively catch and resolve these issues
